facts.fact: Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Samaj in 1828.
Vidyasagar is linked with the Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act 1856.
Sree Narayana Guru gave the slogan 'One caste, one religion, one God'.
Debendranath Tagore founded the Adi Brahmo Samaj (1842).
Keshab Chandra Sen founded the Brahmo Samaj of India (1866).
Dayananda Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj (1875).
Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission (1897).
Sir Syed Ahmad Khan led the Aligarh Movement.
Derozio led the Young Bengal Movement.
Gurajada Apparao wrote Kanyasulkam (1892).
Kandukuri Veeresalingam is the father of the Telugu Renaissance.
Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy led the spoken-Telugu movement.
The Serampore Mission was run by Carey, Marshman and Ward.
The Nellore Baptist mission was the Lone Star Mission.
CMS missionaries worked at Machilipatnam.
Gopal Baba Walangkar published Vital-Vidhvansak.
The Rakhmabai case (1884) touched age of consent and conjugal rights.
The Theosophical Society was founded by Blavatsky and Olcott.
Jyotirao Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj (1873).
M.G. Ranade co-founded the Prarthana Samaj (1867).
Phule wrote Gulamgiri.
Dayananda wrote Satyarth Prakash.
Vivekananda addressed the Chicago Parliament of Religions (1893).
Veeresalingam ran the journal Vivekavardhini.
Vidyasagar was secretary of the Hindu Female School, later the Bethune School (1849).
Ram Mohan Roy's first work was Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin (A Gift to Monotheists), written in Persian.
Ram Mohan Roy founded the Atmiya Sabha at Calcutta in 1815.
Ram Mohan Roy wrote 'Precepts of Jesus' (1820).
Ram Mohan Roy ran Sambad Kaumudi (Bengali) and Mirat-ul-Akhbar (Persian).
Ram Mohan Roy founded the Vedanta College (1825) and helped David Hare found Hindu College (1817).
Mughal emperor Akbar II gave Ram Mohan Roy the title 'Raja'; he died at Bristol in 1833.
Ram Mohan Roy is called the 'Father of the Indian Renaissance' and 'Father of Modern India'.
The Brahmo Sabha was founded on 20 August 1828 and later renamed the Brahmo Samaj.
Radhakanta Deb's Dharma Sabha (1830) defended sati against the reformers.
Debendranath Tagore founded the Tattvabodhini Sabha (1839) and its journal Tattvabodhini Patrika.
Keshab's campaign produced the Native (Brahmo) Marriage Act of 1872, allowing inter-caste marriage.
After Keshab married his minor daughter to the Cooch Behar prince, his followers formed the Sadharan Brahmo Samaj (1878) under Anandamohan Bose and Shivnath Shastri.
Keshab Chandra Sen ran the newspaper 'Indian Mirror'.
Derozio taught at Hindu College, founded the Academic Association and was dismissed in 1831.
Vidyasagar wrote the Bengali primer 'Barna Parichay' and became principal of Sanskrit College.
The first legal Hindu widow remarriage under the 1856 Act took place in Calcutta on 7 December 1856, arranged by Vidyasagar.
Vidyasagar also campaigned against polygamy and child marriage.
The Prarthana Samaj was founded in Bombay (1867) by Atmaram Pandurang, inspired by Keshab Chandra Sen.
The Paramahansa Mandali (1849, Bombay) of Dadoba Pandurang preceded the Prarthana Samaj.
Ranade founded the Indian National Social Conference (1887) and the Widow Remarriage Association (1861).
Ranade helped found the Deccan Education Society (1884).
Jyotirao and Savitribai Phule opened a girls’ school at Bhide Wada, Pune, in 1848.
Jyotirao Phule was given the title 'Mahatma' in 1888; he also wrote 'Sarvajanik Satyadharma'.
Savitribai Phule is regarded as India’s first woman teacher.
D.K. Karve founded a widows’ home (1896) and the SNDT Women’s University (1916).
Pandita Ramabai founded the Arya Mahila Samaj (1882), Sharada Sadan (1889) and the Mukti Mission (Kedgaon); she wrote The High-Caste Hindu Woman.
Gopal Hari Deshmukh 'Lokahitawadi' wrote the Shatapatre (hundred letters) on reform.
Tarabai Shinde wrote 'Stri Purush Tulana' (1882).
Behramji Malabari and Dayaram Gidumal founded the Seva Sadan (Bombay, 1908).
The Age of Consent Act 1891 raised the age of consent for girls from 10 to 12.
The Sarda Act (1929) set the minimum marriage age at 14 for girls and 18 for boys.
Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society (1905).
N.M. Joshi founded the Social Service League (1911).
Margaret Cousins founded the All India Women’s Conference (1927); Annie Besant and Cousins founded the Women’s India Association (1917).
Sarala Devi Chaudhurani founded the Bharat Stree Mahamandal (1910).
Dayananda Saraswati (born Mul Shankar at Tankara, Gujarat, 1824) was a disciple of Swami Virjanand.
The Arya Samaj was founded at Bombay on 10 April 1875; its headquarters moved to Lahore (1877).
The Arya Samaj split (1893): the DAV group (Lala Hansraj, Lajpat Rai) ran DAV College Lahore (1886).
Swami Shraddhanand (Munshi Ram) led the Gurukul group and founded Gurukul Kangri, Haridwar (1902).
Satyarth Prakash was written in Hindi; Dayananda also opposed idol worship and child marriage.
Ramakrishna Paramahamsa (Gadadhar Chattopadhyay) was a priest at the Dakshineswar Kali temple.
Vivekananda was born Narendranath Datta (1863).
Vivekananda spoke at the Chicago Parliament of Religions on 11 September 1893.
The Ramakrishna Mission was founded on 1 May 1897; Belur Math became its headquarters (1899).
Sister Nivedita (Margaret Noble) was an Irish disciple of Vivekananda.
Vivekananda founded the Vedanta Society of New York (1894).
The Ramakrishna movement published Prabuddha Bharata (English) and Udbodhan (Bengali).
Theosophical Society headquarters moved to Adyar, Madras, in 1882 (HQ formally from 1886).
Annie Besant founded the Central Hindu College, Benares (1898), nucleus of BHU.
Annie Besant ran the newspapers New India and Commonwealth.
Annie Besant was the first woman President of the INC (Calcutta, 1917).
Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded the Scientific Society (Ghazipur, 1864).
Sir Syed's journal was Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq.
The MAO College at Aligarh was founded in 1875 and became Aligarh Muslim University in 1920.
The Dar-ul-Uloom at Deoband (1866) was founded by Muhammad Qasim Nanautavi and Rashid Ahmad Gangohi.
The Ahmadiyya movement began at Qadian (Punjab) in 1889.
The Nadwatul Ulama was founded at Lucknow (1894) by Shibli Numani and others.
Nawab Abdul Latif founded the Muhammadan Literary Society at Calcutta (1863).
The Parsi reformers’ journal was Rast Goftar (Truth-Teller).
Baba Dayal Das founded the Nirankari movement among the Sikhs.
The Singh Sabha was founded at Amritsar in 1873; Khalsa College Amritsar followed (1892).
The Akali movement (1920) led to the SGPC and the Sikh Gurdwaras Act (1925); Nankana Sahib saw a massacre in 1921.
The SNDP Yogam was set up in 1903 with Dr Palpu and the poet Kumaran Asan.
The Vaikom Satyagraha (1924–25) for road access near the Vaikom temple was led by T.K. Madhavan and K. Kelappan; Periyar was called Vaikom Veerar.
K. Kelappan led the Guruvayur Satyagraha (1931–32) with A.K. Gopalan.
The Travancore Temple Entry Proclamation was issued on 12 November 1936.
Ayyankali founded the Sadhu Jana Paripalana Sangham (1907) and drove a villuvandi (bullock cart) on public roads (1893).
Vaikunda Swami founded the Samathuva Samajam (1836) in south Travancore.
Mannathu Padmanabhan founded the Nair Service Society (1914); the Malayali Memorial (1891) preceded it.
The South Indian Liberal Federation (1916), called the Justice Party after its paper Justice, was founded by T.M. Nair, P. Tyagaraja Chetti and C.N. Mudaliar.
Periyar's Tamil weekly Kudi Arasu began in 1925 (the PDF says 1910); he formed the Dravidar Kazhagam in 1944.
The Nadar Mahajan Sangam was formed in 1910.
Ambedkar founded the Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha (1924) and the journal Mooknayak (1920).
Gandhi founded the All-India Anti-Untouchability League (1932, later Harijan Sevak Sangh) and the weekly Harijan (1933).
The Kaivartas of Midnapore formed the Jati Nirdharani Sabha (1897) and the Mahishya Samiti (1901).
Guru Ghasidas founded the Satnami movement in Chhattisgarh.
Harichand Thakur founded the Matua sect among the Namasudras of Bengal.
Kandukuri Veeresalingam was born at Rajahmundry in 1848.
Veeresalingam started Vivekavardhini (1874) and a girls’ school at Dowlaiswaram (1874).
The first widow remarriage he arranged took place at Rajahmundry on 11 December 1881.
Rajasekhara Charitramu (1878), based on The Vicar of Wakefield, is regarded as the first Telugu novel.
Veeresalingam founded the Hitakarini Samaj (1906) and wrote the first Telugu autobiography.
Veeresalingam was called 'Gadya Tikkana' and ran Satihitabodhini, a journal for women.
Gurajada Apparao worked at the court of the Maharaja of Vizianagaram; he also wrote Mutyala Saralu.
Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy was born on 29 August 1863 and started the journal Telugu (1919).
Gidugu wrote a grammar of the Savara tribal language and received the Kaisar-i-Hind medal (1913).
Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu was principal of Pithapuram Raja College, Kakinada, and was called Brahmarshi.
Chilakamarthi Lakshmi Narasimham, the blind 'Andhra Milton', wrote Gayopakhyanam.
Komarraju Venkata Lakshmana Rao founded the Vignana Chandrika Mandali (1906).
Unnava Lakshminarayana wrote Malapalli (1922) and founded Sarada Niketan for women at Guntur.
Bhagya Reddy Varma led the Adi Hindu movement for Dalits in Hyderabad (Jagan Mitra Mandali, 1906).
Gurram Jashuva's poem Gabbilam (The Bat) protested untouchability.
Chembeti Sridharalu Naidu founded the Veda Samaj at Madras (1864), inspired by Keshab; it became the Brahmo Samaj of South India (1871).
Durgabai Deshmukh founded the Andhra Mahila Sabha (1937).
